summary: Oregon watershed lookout near Corvallis, built 1940-41 with lookouts in tents first; removed by 1968. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed by 1968. No source describes what remains at the butte today.

events.note: Construction of a 52-foot tower with a 14x14-foot house announced in July (Corvallis Gazette-Times, July 24, 1940); reported nearly complete in September (Sept. 18, 1940)
Lookouts on duty at the butte, housed in tents
Register gives 1941 and a 41-foot treated timber live-in tower; first used in 1941 (Gazette-Times, July 3, 1941)
Gone by 1968 (register, firelookout.com); the Oregon history lists it as Removed without a year

evidence.supports: tower for protection of the Corvallis watershed on the east slope of Mary's Peak
evidence.quote: protection of the Corvallis watershed area on the east slope of Mary's Peak

evidence.supports: July 24, 1940: lookout announced to protect the Corvallis watershed
evidence.quote: July 24, 1940: Construction of a fire lookout tower on Pioneer Butte for protection of the Corvallis watershed area

evidence.supports: Siuslaw National Forest supervisor announced the lookout
evidence.quote: Dahl Kirkpatrick, Siuslaw National forest supervisor, announced today.

evidence.supports: plan for a 14 by 14 house on a 52-foot tower
evidence.quote: A 14 by 14 foot house will be constructed atop a 52 foot wooden tower
September 18, 1940: Construction of a lookout on Pioneer butte in the Peak area is just about completed.

evidence.supports: July 3, 1941: first use of the tower; lookouts in tents the year before
evidence.quote: July 3, 1941: The new lookout towers on Alsea mountain and Pioneer Butte in the Peak area are being used for the first time, though lookouts were on duty there last year housed in tents.
Built in 1941, this 41' treated timber live-in tower was gone by 1968.

evidence.supports: register field: administered by Oregon Dept. of Forestry

corrections.why: The register gives a 41-foot treated timber tower (about 12.5 m). The 4.3 m value matches no cited source. The 1940 plan says 52 feet, so a human should check which height the record means.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1940 newspapers report construction and near completion; 1941 is the first season the tower was used, and the register gives 1941 as the build year.
The register lists the Oregon Department of Forestry; the 1940 announcement came from the Siuslaw National Forest supervisor. The sources do not say how the two were connected.

sources.title: Pioneer Butte Lookout Site (US 725), Former Fire Lookout Sites Register
Pioneer Butte, Forest Lookouts of Oregon

notes_for_editor: The height in the record (4.3 m) matches no cited source; a correction is proposed for human review. Build year (1940 construction vs 1941 register) and agency (Oregon Dept. of Forestry in the register vs the Siuslaw National Forest in the 1940 announcement) conflict, and the story reports both. One web search for the butte's current condition returned nothing relevant. The register has a 1944 photo and a 2008 site photo, both courtesy of Howard Verschoor; these were not fetched or added. Verification 2026-10-09: the story now credits both the register and firelookout.com for the 41-foot tower; the Mary's Peak location and the 1940 and 1941 dates are now carried in dated quotes from the Corvallis Gazette-Times reprints on the Oregon history page.
